patterns.usage_note: Grants or asks permission (出社してもいいですよ), and after a noun (これでいい) concedes that a lesser option is acceptable rather than merely permitted. Its class siblings are てもかまわない, which voices indifference rather than approval, and ても差し支えない, the formal one. This is the neutral everyday form between equals and downward; upward, ask rather than grant, and raise the politeness: 〜てもよろしいでしょうか.

examples.ruby: 熱[ねつ]がないなら、明日[あす]から出社[しゅっしゃ]してもいいですよ。
examples.english: If your fever's gone, feel free to come back to the office tomorrow.

examples.ruby: 冷[さ]めないうちに、先[さき]に飲[の]んでもいい。
examples.english: Go ahead and start drinking before it gets cold.

examples.ruby: バットは重[おも]いから、短[みじか]く持[も]ってもいいよ。
examples.english: The bat's heavy, so it's fine to choke up on it.

glosses: I don't mind if; it doesn't matter if
may, as far as I'm concerned
patterns.usage_note: Says the speaker has no objection: 構わない is "it doesn't bother me", so this expresses tolerance or indifference rather than the approval of its sibling てもいい (どこに座ってもかまいません). Asked as てもかまいませんか it is the more deferential of the two and the safer form with a superior, though granted as permission it can sound faintly grudging. The ん / ぬ / ねえ endings in this family are blunt or dialectal.

examples.ruby: 席[せき]は空[あ]いていますので、どこに座[すわ]ってもかまいません。
examples.english: There are plenty of seats free, so sit wherever you like.

examples.ruby: 多少[たしょう]高[たか]くてもかまわないから、丈夫[じょうぶ]な靴[くつ]がほしい。
examples.english: I don't care if it costs a bit more, I want shoes that will last.

examples.ruby: 洗[あら]ってあるので、そのまま手[て]で食[た]べてもかまいません。
examples.english: They've already been washed, so feel free to eat them straight from your hand.

patterns.canonical_surface: だってさしつかえない
glosses: there is no objection to; it is quite all right to
patterns.usage_note: Rules out a practical obstacle: 差し支える is "to get in the way", so this states that an action causes no problem rather than encouraging it (代理の方が受け取っても差し支えない). It is the formal member of this class, used where a rule, deadline, or procedure is at issue, against everyday てもいい and tolerant てもかまわない. In polite finite position 差し支えありません is more usual than this ない form.

examples.ruby: 会場[かいじょう]の写真[しゃしん]は撮[と]っても差[さ]し支[つか]えないでしょうか。
examples.english: Would there be any objection to my photographing the venue?

examples.ruby: 担当者[たんとうしゃ]が不在[ふざい]なら、代理[だいり]の方[かた]が受[う]け取[と]っても差[さ]し支[つか]えない。
examples.english: If the person in charge is out, there is no objection to a proxy accepting it.

examples.ruby: 軽[かる]い運動[うんどう]なら、来週[らいしゅう]から始[はじ]めても差[さ]し支[つか]えない。
examples.english: As long as it is light exercise, there is no problem starting next week.
